# Data dictionary

*Generated by `scripts/build_data_dictionary.py`. Do not edit by hand —*
*edit `sql/star_schema.sql` or `hourglass.phi.FIELD_CLASSIFICATION` and*
*regenerate. A hand-maintained dictionary is accurate the day it is*
*written and misleading a month later.*

Every column carries a data-protection classification. That column is not
documentation: `hourglass.phi.check_egress` reads the same table, and a
column that is missing from it or classified as a direct identifier will
stop the pipeline from publishing. **All data described here is synthetic.**

## Classifications

| Classification | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `direct_identifier` | **Never published raw.** Pseudonymised on export. |
| `quasi_identifier` | Published, but generalised where it can be. |
| `clinical` | Health information. Published only alongside pseudonymised keys. |
| `operational` | About the business, not the person. |
| `safe` | Reference data with no link to an individual. |

A column absent from the classification table is treated as a direct
identifier. Unknown is not safe, and the default has to fail loudly.

## `dim_client`

**Grain.** one row per client per version of that client's record. Slowly Changing Dimension, Type 2. A client whose payer changed has two rows with adjacent, non-overlapping validity ranges. Facts join to the row that was in effect on the event date, so history stays attributed to the payer who was actually responsible at the time.

**Lineage.** salesforce_clients.csv → `build_dim_client` (SCD Type 2)

## `fact_authorization`

**Grain.** one row per authorisation line -- one client, one service, one period. Note the two date keys. An authorisation is not an event on a day, it is a permission spanning a range, so it carries a start and an end rather than a single date_key. This is why it cannot share a grain with fact_session.  The grain carries an assumption the schema cannot enforce: for one client and one service, the periods must not intersect. Every roll-up in this project attributes a session by client, service and date BETWEEN the two keys, so a session inside an overlap is counted in full against both authorisations. No constraint here can express "these two ranges must not intersect", and real payers amend and reissue, so the rule is enforced where it can be: quality.check_overlapping_authorization_periods, at BLOCK.

**Lineage.** payer_authorizations.csv → `build_fact_authorization`

**Rows in the current warehouse.** 1,825

| Column | Type | Classification | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auth_id` | TEXT | `direct_identifier` | **Never published raw.** Pseudonymised on export. |
| `client_key` | INTEGER | `operational` | About the business, not the person. |
| `service_key` | INTEGER | `clinical` | Health information. Published only alongside pseudonymised keys. |
| `payer_key` | INTEGER | `operational` | About the business, not the person. |
| `period_start_key` | INTEGER | `quasi_identifier` | Published, but generalised where it can be. |
| `period_end_key` | INTEGER | `quasi_identifier` | Published, but generalised where it can be. |
| `units_authorized` | REAL | `clinical` | Health information. Published only alongside pseudonymised keys. |
| `authorized_days` | INTEGER | `operational` | About the business, not the person. |

## `fact_session`

**Grain.** one row per delivered therapy session. uom_resolved is a measure-quality flag, not a business attribute. Rows where it is 0 have a duration whose unit of measure could not be determined; their measures are zero and they are excluded from utilisation. Keeping the rows rather than dropping them means the size of the hole is queryable.

**Lineage.** ehr_sessions.csv → `dedupe_sessions` → `resolve_minutes` → `build_fact_session`

## `run_log`

**Grain.** one row per pipeline run, published or blocked. Append-only. The rule-set hash matters: without it the log records that checks passed but not which version of the checks, and an old verdict could be mistaken for a statement about the current rules.  Blocked runs belong here as much as published ones. For a while they did not: a blocked run's row went only to the quarantined warehouse, which the next blocked run overwrote, so the log held nothing but successes and read as if the gate had never fired. `pipeline.append_run_log_row` is what puts them back; the columns below are the same either way, with `published = 0`.  refused_acknowledgements records the releases that were attempted and denied. Somebody trying to sign off a PHI failure is a more interesting event than any successful release, and it used to survive only in a quality report the next run overwrote.

**Lineage.** written by `model.atomic_build` on every run

**Rows.** Grows by one per pipeline run and is never truncated, so the count is a property of this machine's run history rather than of the data. Omitted here so the generated file is reproducible.

| Column | Type | Classification | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | TEXT | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `started_at_utc` | TEXT | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `finished_at_utc` | TEXT | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `code_version` | TEXT | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `ruleset_version` | TEXT | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `ruleset_hash` | TEXT | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `published` | INTEGER | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `blocking_failures` | TEXT | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `acknowledgements` | TEXT | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `refused_acknowledgements` | TEXT | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `session_rows` | INTEGER | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `auth_rows` | INTEGER | n/a | Internal table; never published. |
| `lake_backend` | TEXT | n/a | Internal table; never published. |

## Service catalogue

`minutes_per_unit` is the reason `dim_service` exists. A "unit" is not a
fixed quantity of time, so a units column cannot be summed across service
codes without this conversion — and every hours figure in the project,
Python, SQL and DAX alike, converts through it.

| Code | Service | Discipline | Unit basis | Minutes per unit |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| `97151` | Behavior identification assessment | ABA | `15_min` | 15 |
| `97153` | Adaptive behavior treatment by protocol | ABA | `15_min` | 15 |
| `97155` | Adaptive behavior treatment w/ protocol modification | ABA | `15_min` | 15 |
| `97156` | Family adaptive behavior treatment guidance | ABA | `15_min` | 15 |
| `92507` | Speech/language treatment | Speech | `per_session` | 45 |
| `97530` | Therapeutic activities (OT) | Occupational | `15_min` | 15 |
| `99213` | Office visit, established patient | Medical | `per_session` | 30 |

## What is deliberately not modelled

- **Authorisation amendments.** Authorisations are modelled as issued, not
  as revised. Real payers amend them, and a Type 2 `fact_authorization`
  would be the way to carry that.
- **Session start times.** The source has none, which is why the
  deduplication key cannot distinguish a genuine second visit on the same
  day from a double entry. See `transform.dedupe_sessions`.
- **Provider history.** `dim_provider` is Type 1; corrections overwrite.
  Client history is load-bearing for payer attribution, provider history is
  not, and the complexity was not worth it here.
